correctness.rationale: At finite n, the 4-type state has exactly three allowed-edge categories with counts xv,uy,uv. Density-dependent martingale quadratic variation is O(T/n) for each fixed T, and the drift is Lipschitz. The explicit scalar W transformation has a first positive zero W*=log(beta/alpha)/(beta-alpha), or W*=1/alpha on the diagonal, yielding positive terminal bad density L. The terminal sandwich between X_n(T)-V_n(T) and X_n(T)+U_n(T) handles infinite time. Hall feasibility is equivalent to a_n+b_n<=n. The integral representation log L=average(g), g(s)=log s+1-1/s, and strict concavity/monotonicity establish L<=1/(2e), with unique equality at alpha=beta=1/2. The supplied verifier ran successfully with exact small-state terminal probabilities; program tests are subsidiary to the analytic proof.

value.rationale: The same deterministic graph has perfect matchings throughout a+b<=n, yet a uniform irreversible greedy dimer process leaves Theta(n) uncovered vertices, whose exact fraction depends nontrivially on two blocked proportions. The sharp 1/(2e) global feasible-block extremum isolates a natural worst jamming configuration and makes a measurable prediction about kinetic inefficiency that is not a simple Hall or matching-number deduction.
